          The 10% Club: Opta's Best Under-the-Radar FPL Picks for Gameweek 7
        
      
                          
                      Oct 15, 2026
          
                      Tom Patey / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Looking for an under-the-radar pick in Fantasy Premier League? The 10% Club has you covered for FPL Gameweek 7.
Tempted by a triple Chelsea attack; considering moving away from double Arsenal defence; or still expecting Brighton’s run of form to end?
Those may be just a few of many questions floating through the minds of Fantasy Premier League managers as Gameweek 7 approaches. But, as always, we’re to help.
Using Opta data, we’ve picked out five under-the-radar stars – all owned by fewer than 10% of managers – to help go against the FPL template this weekend.
Tottenham may be winless this campaign, but an improved performance in their draw away to Manchester United may give Roberto De Zerbi hope.

Coventry are their next visitors, and although Frank Lampard’s side backed up their first win over Nottingham Forest with a 4-1 thrashing of Newcastle United, De Zerbi will clearly see this as a good opportunity to get Spurs on track.
A lack of attacking options, with Spurs scoring just three goals so far, pushes us towards looking at their defence, where Jan Paul van Hecke continues to shine.
The Dutch defender’s 27 points are the most of any Tottenham player. He's registered DEFCON returns twice in 2026-27 and also scored in his last home outing in GW5.
Van Hecke also seems to be Spurs’ set-piece target. His 1.1 expected goal involvements are only bettered by Dominic Solanke (1.3) and Sávio (1.5) among all of De Zerbi’s squad in the competition.
Although Van Hecke travels to free-scoring Chelsea next weekend, a favourable run then sees Spurs face Palace, Ipswich Town and Fulham in their next three home games.
Not many sides have a better upcoming swing of fixtures before the November international break, and if De Zerbi can get Spurs firing, Van Hecke’s 6.3% ownership will only soar.
Brighton duo Pascal Groẞ and Maxim De Cuyper continue to lead the way, with their 53 points each the most of any player this season.
Bart Verbruggen is another to impress, with the third-most points of all goalkeepers (32). But the Brighton trio are all in more than 10% of squads ahead their home fixture with Crystal Palace.

However, Luka Vuskovic continues to go under the radar. His 40 points put him fifth on the list of all defenders, and three of the four above him (Joško Gvardiol, James Tarkowski and De Cuyper) are all owned by a significant proportion of managers.

The Croatian defender has hit the threshold for defensive contributions in 50% of his matches. However, those DEFCON returns could easily have increased if Coventry City and Aston Villa hadn’t received red cards to dampen their attacking threat.
Vuskovic has also picked up a clean sheet in four of six league outings, while he scored against Leeds United for a mega 12-point haul on GW3.

His attacking threat, largely from set-pieces, shouldn’t be a surprise. Only Alejandro Grimaldo, who scored eight times as Bayer Leverkusen’s attacking full-back, could better Vuskovic’s six Bundesliga goals among all defenders last season.

Despite tough upcoming trips to Liverpool and Manchester City, those visits only heighten Vuskovic’s DEFCON appeal. Plus, a clean sheet isn’t completely off the cards considering Brighton’s 3-0 dismantling of Arsenal on GW5.
Despite waiting until GW5 for his first start, only Emiliano Buendía (25) and John McGinn (27) have more points than Johan Manzambi’s 19 for Aston Villa.

The Switzerland international has two assists and one goal in his first two Premier League starts, racking up 13 points against Tottenham before adding five more against Brentford with his assist for McGinn.
